what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes; it heard the FY24 general government, health, unclassified and debt service budgets, which show a decrease in debt service with no new borrowing.
Schools presented their School Committee-approved FY24 budget and withdrew two requests: the in-house IT position and the high school dean position.
Monty Tech presented its assessment, including a statement that the Governor's budget projects an increase to Chapter 70 and Student Opportunity Act funding.
The chair is to work on the finance committee warrant report, which must be voted by the 30th.
The committee agreed to meet April 6 and to decide next week whether to hold an additional public hearing later in April.

why_it_matters: The school and town budgets that will reach Town Meeting were presented here but not yet voted, so the amounts residents will be asked to approve are still open to change.
Withdrawing the IT and dean positions lowers the school request as presented, but the minutes give no figure for the effect on the tax bill.
watch_next: The finance committee warrant report, which must be voted by the 30th.
The committee's decision next week on an additional public hearing in April, and the April 6 meeting.

reconciliation.summary: Neither record has a non-procedural vote or a transfer, and the figures they share (select board hours, insurance, salary reserve, Monty Tech Chapter 70, LED, Municibid, master plan) match. The one thing to know: our minutes record four decisions (two withdrawn school positions, an April 6 meeting, the warrant report) and the official minutes record none, and our minutes also carry much of the Monty Tech and school budget discussion that the official minutes leave out.
